title: Tubogas Dome Ring
category: Ring (closed, sized tubogas dome band, no stones, no clasp; sold as 1 piece; US 6, 7 and 8 in stock in both metals, US 5 listed but sold out)
metal: Two variants: 18k gold tone (PVD 18K gold) or rhodium silver tone (PVD rhodium), both over surgical stainless steel, 'anti-tarnish' (listing). Finish: high mirror polish on every ridge, fine dark gaps between the ridges, no brushing, no hammering, no engraving, no stones. Photos by metal: every live listing photo is 18k gold tone (01 macro, 02 worn, 04 size guide; 03 is the box). There is no live rhodium silver tone photo: the only true-proportion silver source is the supplier photo /home/user/naira-scroll/docs/creative/edition-two-listings/pi-refs/P01_silver.jpg (local only, silver ring stacked on a gold one). This card shoots 18k gold tone.
lock: 1 closed seamless ring of flexible tubogas: 0 stones, 0 clasp, 0 gap. A slim band 5.8 mm wide along the finger, about 3 mm thick, its outer face a puffed rounded dome. About 60 fine polished ridges follow one another all the way round, each running straight across the band's width (parallel to the finger), evenly spaced about 1.3 mm apart, fine dark gaps between. 18k gold tone, mirror polish. Must stay a slim 5.8 mm band with its ridges running across it, never a wide cigar band, a bangle or a spiral spring.
morph: Band width, first and by far. This piece has already been redesigned wide once by an image model: the Edition Two hero and silver packshots (edition-two-listings/exports/tubogas-dome-ring-01.jpg and -04.jpg) were generated as a 9-10 mm cigar band, the copy followed ('about 10mm across the finger'), and the listing was corrected on 21 Oct 2026 to 5.8 mm with the supplier photo as the size guide. The still-live macro 01 and the old E2 ad (finished-ads/e2/out/E2_tubogas_a1.jpg, 'Chudiyan, on silent', Rs 1,399) still show the wide version, and a tight crop with no referent turns it into a bangle or cuff (01 reads exactly like one). Second: ridge direction. Models wind the ridges into 1 helical spring, a coiled phone cord or a twisted rope, or turn them to run round the ring like a stack of thin bands (prompting 'a churi stack' invites this). The ridges are separate, parallel, and cross the band. Third: the dome flattened into a flat band, or a seam, hinge, clasp, opening or stones added.
sizeMm: Listed: band approximately 5.8 mm wide (description; size guide 04: 'Band 5.8 mm wide, US 5, 6, 7, 8', 'give or take 1 mm'); weight approximately 2.7 g; US 5, 6, 7, 8 (US 5 has 0 stock in both metals). Standard US chart inside diameters: US 6 about 16.5 mm, US 7 about 17.3 mm, US 8 about 18.1 mm. Estimated, not listed: wall about 3 mm thick; outer about 23-25 mm across (measured on 04 against its own 5.8 mm marker: about 24.8 mm, perspective approximate); about 60 ridges at about 1.3 mm pitch (front-centre pitch 27 px against 20.7 px/mm; never print a ridge count). Body referents: worn (02), the band is about a third as wide as the finger is across and sits between knuckle and base like a slim band, not knuckle to knuckle; a little narrower than a pencil is thick (about 7 mm); outer about the size of a Rs 2 to Rs 5 coin (23-25 mm); the opening is about the size of a 1-rupee coin's face (20 mm) or a little smaller.

story: What is lovable: one shape, a lot of light. There are no stones, yet each of the band's polished ridges throws its own thin line of highlight, so the ring glitters in a row of tiny mirrors like a pave band, at the price of plain metal. It flexes as the hand bends (the listing's own 'move like an accordion'), which is a motion hook, and at 5.8 mm it is a daily ring: alone on the index finger, or beside a slim plain band (the listing's styling tip). Heritage worth knowing: tubogas is Italian for 'gas pipe', the 1920s-50s technique of winding metal into a flexible ribbed tube with no solder. Name the technique, never a house. Rhymes that keep the ridges running the right way, across the band: saree pleats (pleats that never fall out, that never need a safety pin; a mother's hand mid-pleat, the ring on her pleating finger); harmonium bellows at a sangeet (the folds open as she plays: 'Sa re ga ma, on one finger'; fits c03); a bendy straw's accordion neck in a nimbu pani; the pleated gold-foil cups in a mithai box (a kaju katli in each, the ring as the smallest cup); a fluted cutting-chai glass seen from above (the ring rests on its rim, flute for flute); a roll of coins; a Slinky bent into an O; the gangway bellows between two train coaches; a gold caterpillar curled into a ring; an armadillo (armour for one finger); a tiny spine that bends where you bend. Crazy-camp fits: c06 KAHAN SE LIYA? (the ring is the 0 in '0 stones', or the full stop); c02 LAST PRICE? (Rs 999 inside its 17 mm opening, true scale, tiny type); c10 NOT A GIANT HOOP (in a 1:50 room it becomes a 1.2 m gold ribbed round ottoman or a tunnel, true size the whole time); c08 THE ONLY COLOUR (the one gold thing in a black-and-white wedding); c07 BAS, EK AUR (the stage hand). Sound and motion: a fingernail dragged across the ridges gives a zipper-like tick (an ASMR open); a slow fist makes the ridges fan. Rhymes to avoid: anything ridged lengthwise (chakli or murukku, a churro, a stack of churis, a coiled phone cord, a spring, a shower hose) pulls the model into running the ridges round the ring or into a helix. The old E2 ad ran 'Chudiyan, on silent' and 'A churi stack, for one finger' on a 10 mm render at Rs 1,399: stale scale and stale price.
